history.dynasty: Karvetinagaram (Karveti Nagara) kings; taken over by Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD) on 23 September 1988
history.period: Sthalapurana is legendary; widely reported construction date 1232 AD by Sri Venkata Perumalaraju Brahmadeva Maharaj of Karvetinagaram
history.summary: One of the seven ancient Venkateswara temples around Tirumala, at Appalayagunta village about 16-20 km from Tirupati. Legend: after marrying Padmavathi at Narayanavanam, Lord Venkateswara rested here on the way to Tirumala and promised Siddheswara muni he would stay and bless devotees; Siddheswara installed the idol down the hill and the Lord is named 'Prasanna Venkateswara' (the ever-gracious Lord), shown in the rare Abhaya Hasta (right hand in blessing posture) unlike the usual Varada posture. A big pond (Amruta Sarovaram; 'Appalaya Gunta' etymology from daily wage payments to coolies) fronts the temple. Scripture-based accounts credit Karvetinagaram kings with construction, with a reported date of 1232 AD under Sri Venkata Perumalaraju Brahmadeva Maharaj (verify; one account says temple is ~1000 years old and renovated c.1750). TTD took over administration on 23 September 1988; a rajagopuram was added later. CSV ERRORS: the CSV 'state' column contains 'Chittoor' (a district name), not a state; the correct state is Andhra Pradesh. The CSV town/district 'Chittoor' is also imprecise: the village is in Tirupati district (formed 2022; earlier Chittoor district); sources differ between 'Chittoor district' and 'Tirupati district' (verify). HOURS CONFLICT: reported timings differ (6 AM-8 PM with no midday closure vs 5:45 AM-8 PM; Sarva Darshan 6:30 AM-7:30 PM with 1:30-3 PM break) - verify.

name: Sri Venkateswara Temple, Appalayagunta
town_description: Appalayagunta is a small village in Tirupati district, Andhra Pradesh, about 16-20 km northeast of Tirupati and about 12 km from Tiruchanur, set against a high hill with fields around. It is known chiefly for this TTD-administered Venkateswara temple, one of the seven ancient temples around Tirumala, drawing devotees seeking a calmer alternative to the crowded Tirumala shrine.
